description: verify-loops.sh, the script whose entire purpose is proving real side-effects, never checks a live URL for either capafy or reddit despite the claim requiring exactly that ('a real published skill URL', 'a real posted Reddit comment URL'). For capafy it extracts only a `title` field from the last published.jsonl line; for reddit it only counts lines in posts.jsonl and reports mtime freshness. Neither branch reads a `url` field or curls it to confirm the artifact is actually live. Both checks reduce to 'does a log line exist and is it recent' -- i.e. trusting the same actor's self-report, not an independent observation.

evidence.snippet:
echo "[capafy]  published.jsonl: $CNT skills total | newest: $(fresh "$PUB") | last title: $(tail -1 "$PUB" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.loads(sys.stdin.read()).get("title","?")[:45])' ...)"
...
NPOST=$(grep -c . "$POSTS" 2>/dev/null||echo 0)
echo "[reddit]  accounts: $NACC | posts logged: $NPOST | posts ledger: $(fresh "$POSTS")"

concreteFailureScenario: The capafy publish pipeline appends a line to published.jsonl with a title but the listing was actually rejected by Capafy moderation seconds later; verify-loops.sh still reports it as a fresh, counted 'published' skill because it never checks a URL or re-queries Capafy for the listing's live status. Same for reddit: a stale/placeholder or dead-link URL logged in posts.jsonl would read identically to a genuinely live posted comment.
